claims.text: The preserved source requires only a Top100 solution at thousand-hundred-million scale; largest/smallest, distinctness, type, ordering, storage, and API are not specified.

Under the explicit largest-K-with-duplicates sequential-input contract, the exact candidate Java fence matches an independent full-sort oracle across exhaustive, randomized, duplicate, extreme, and K-boundary cases.
Under the same contract, taking local TopK per partition and then TopK over the local candidates preserves the direct global TopK.
The implementation performs one sequential pass and maintains at most K heap values, so CPU time is O(n log K) with O(K) auxiliary memory, excluding source I/O.

findings: The preserved repository source says only “算法：千亿数组Top100”; it does not specify largest versus smallest, distinctness, element type, result ordering, storage topology, or API.

The candidate preserves that sparse source boundary and explicitly labels largest values, duplicate-preserving multiset semantics, sequential long input, descending result order, and Java as answer-side contracts rather than source facts.

The min-heap invariant is correct: after each consumed prefix, a full heap contains the largest K values from that prefix under the declared multiset contract, with the root as the weakest retained candidate.
Dropping a value equal to the current heap minimum remains correct for value-multiset TopK because replacing one retained threshold value by an equal value leaves the result multiset unchanged.

The complete Java class is runnable, returns descending output, handles K=0 and K larger than the input, preserves duplicate values, and its O(n log K) time plus O(K) auxiliary-space claims match the implementation.

Reviewer-owned validation extracts the exact candidate Java fence and compares it with an independent full-sort oracle across all 19,531 arrays of length 0..6 over values -2..2 for K=0..8, 5,000 seeded randomized cases, long extremes, and declared invalid-input boundaries.

A separate 1,000-case randomized partition test confirms the stated mergeability property: local TopK candidates from every partition are sufficient to reconstruct the direct global TopK under the same declared contract.
No fabricated production experience, placeholder implementation, cross-topic contamination, or uncovered source variant was found.
